_metadata.independence: Apart from the brief, I read only x22-re-input.json; no other repository file, search, web or API was used.

hints.reason: AMERICA via liberty as a founding ideal and the Statue of Liberty; BELL via the Liberty Bell, an instantly familiar American icon.

pairs.pair_note: Solid, easy patriotic link; both sides land at once.

hints.reason: BALANCE via the gymnastics balance beam (a wooden beam); LASER via a beam of light, two different senses of beam.

pairs.pair_note: Clean double meaning, wood beam vs light beam.

hints.reason: BASEBALL via the batter at the plate; BEAT via cake batter that is beaten, with the bonus that to batter also means to beat repeatedly.

pairs.pair_note: Three-way pun (baseball batter, cake batter, to batter = to beat); a strong clue.

hints.reason: BED via the queen-size mattress; BEE via the queen bee of a honeybee colony.

pairs.pair_note: Classic and fair; lines are carefully worded.

hints.reason: BIRTHDAY via a birthday present (gift); PAST via the present as the time after the past.

pairs.pair_note: Textbook double meaning with a satisfying click.

hints.reason: BLUE via the color royal blue (instant); JELLY via royal jelly, the bee secretion sold as a supplement, which is familiar to many but not all U.S. players.

pairs.pair_note: Phrase-join that passes on royal blue's familiarity; royal jelly is the softer side, so a second opinion is reasonable.

hints.reason: BOTTLE via the classic ship in a bottle; SAIL via ships with sails (sailing ships), which is also what those models depict.

pairs.pair_note: Coherent single image (a tall ship in a bottle); easy but pleasant.

hints.reason: BREAD via mold growing on stale bread; SHAPE via to mold, meaning to shape.

pairs.pair_note: Clean noun/verb double meaning.

hints.reason: CAR via a car dealer; DECK via the card dealer who shuffles and deals the deck.

pairs.pair_note: Fair double meaning; both senses very familiar.

hints.reason: THIEF via bandit as a robber; CASINO via the slot machine nickname one-armed bandit.

pairs.pair_note: Synonym on one side, but the one-armed bandit gives a genuine aha on the other.

hints.reason: CHAIN via Jacob Marley's chain-laden ghost in A Christmas Carol; DOG via the Labrador of the hit book and film Marley & Me.

pairs.pair_note: Two well-known Marleys; players may think Bob Marley first, but both target routes are mainstream and click once seen. Worth a second opinion on familiarity.

hints.reason: CHESS via the rook piece; TOWER via the rook's castle-tower shape (it is also called the castle).
hints.fix: The chess rook is usually shaped like a castle tower.

pairs.pair_note: Fair and familiar; TOWER line says carved, but most sets are molded plastic, so soften it. CASTLE is a reasonable alternative, not clearly better.

hints.reason: JET via the Boeing 747 jumbo jet; CIRCUS via Jumbo, P. T. Barnum's famous elephant (echoed by Mrs. Jumbo in Dumbo).

pairs.pair_note: Lovely: the word jumbo itself comes from the circus elephant.

hints.reason: CLOUD via the saying every cloud has a silver lining; COAT via the fabric lining sewn inside.

pairs.pair_note: Idiom plus literal sense; fair and pleasant.

hints.reason: COOL via the Cool Ranch Doritos flavor; FARM via a ranch as a livestock farm.

pairs.pair_note: Brand plus near-synonym; Cool Ranch makes it fun.

hints.reason: SCALE via do, re, mi as the first solfege notes; DEER via the song's famous doe, a female deer pun.
hints.fix: The song's best-known verse begins by punning on doe, a female deer.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; the song literally starts with the deer line. Small fix: the song's very first line is the 'start at the very beginning' intro, not the doe line.

hints.reason: HISTORY via medical history and DOCTOR via medical doctor are both real, but the adjective is a flat category label with no aha, the weakest phrase-join in the batch.

pairs.pair_note: Accurate and fair but unremarkable; I could not find a clearly better one-word hint, so this is a taste call (PASS as an easy clue is defensible).

hints.reason: DRINK via the powdered drink mix; WALL via the Kool-Aid Man crashing through walls in ads.

pairs.pair_note: Iconic mascot gag; very satisfying.

hints.reason: EINSTEIN via his years at the Swiss patent office in Bern; SHOE via glossy patent leather shoes.

pairs.pair_note: Indirect familiar-knowledge aha in the owner's favoured style.

hints.reason: FIELD via field trip; SCHOOL via school trip, and the two phrases name the same outing.

pairs.pair_note: Phrase-join that converges on one thing (a field trip is a school trip); easy but satisfying.

hints.reason: FISHING via a fishing pole; MAGNET via its north and south poles.

pairs.pair_note: Clean double meaning.

hints.reason: MASK via the masked hero Zorro; FOX via zorro being Spanish for fox, widely known in the U.S.

pairs.pair_note: Strong aha; the Spanish meaning is the hero's own name origin.

hints.reason: GAME via the Netflix hit Squid Game; OCTOPUS via the squid as a fellow cephalopod.

pairs.pair_note: Title plus category relative; fair and current.

hints.reason: GHOST via phantom as a ghost; THEATER via The Phantom of the Opera, set in a Paris opera house and a landmark stage musical.
hints.fix: The Phantom of the Opera haunts a Paris opera house and became Broadway's longest-running show.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; the THEATER line uses present tense for the Broadway run, which closed in 2023, so it needs a tense fix.

hints.reason: HAMBURGER via flipping burgers on the grill; SWITCH via flipping a light switch.

pairs.pair_note: Easy shared verb; fair.

hints.reason: HONEY via Pooh's love of honey; ROBIN via Christopher Robin, the boy whose bear Pooh is.
hints.fix: Pooh is the teddy bear of the boy Christopher Robin.

pairs.pair_note: Lovely; the ROBIN line's 'best friend' is an unsupported superlative (Piglet is often called Pooh's best friend).

hints.reason: TURKEY via the turkey drumstick (lower leg); ICE CREAM via the Drumstick brand of chocolate-and-nut-topped cones.

pairs.pair_note: Strong brand-plus-literal double meaning.

hints.reason: KING via a king as a ruler of a realm; LINE via the measuring ruler used to draw straight lines.

pairs.pair_note: Classic, crisp double meaning.

hints.reason: LEGO via sets built from plastic pieces (piece counts on every box); PUZZLE via jigsaw pieces.

pairs.pair_note: Plain but honest and clear; generic is not a reason to reject.

hints.reason: MAGNET via magnetic attraction; PARK via theme-park attractions.

pairs.pair_note: Neat science/leisure double meaning.

hints.reason: MUD via adobe bricks of sun-dried mud; PHOTO via Adobe, maker of Photoshop.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent brand-versus-material aha.

hints.reason: NINJA via Master Splinter, sensei of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles; WOOD via a splinter as a sliver of wood.

pairs.pair_note: Strong character-plus-literal pairing.

hints.reason: PAINTING via Leonardo da Vinci and the Mona Lisa; SWORD via the Ninja Turtle Leonardo's twin katanas.

pairs.pair_note: Great two-Leonardos aha; note it shares the TMNT family with SPLINTER, so avoid both on one board.

hints.reason: PHOTO via a photo album; RECORD via a record album.

pairs.pair_note: Instantly familiar phrase-join; easy and fair.

hints.reason: PINK via Nintendo's round pink hero Kirby; VACUUM via the Kirby vacuum brand, doubled by Kirby inhaling enemies like a vacuum.

pairs.pair_note: Double-strength vacuum side; very satisfying.

hints.reason: STORM via Star Wars stormtroopers; POLICE via state troopers.

pairs.pair_note: Compound plus real meaning; strong pop-culture aha.

hints.reason: PRINCESS via The Princess and the Pea fairy tale; SOUP via split pea soup.

pairs.pair_note: Fairy tale plus food; fun and fair.

hints.reason: SHORT via a short circuit; RACE via a racing circuit such as Formula One tracks.

pairs.pair_note: Fair double meaning; racing circuit is slightly less everyday in the U.S. than track but well known.

hints.reason: TEAM via crew as a working team; ROW via crew as the U.S. name for competitive rowing.

pairs.pair_note: Synonym on one side, real second sense on the other; fine.

hints.reason: SHEEP via counting sheep to fall asleep; VAMPIRE via Count Dracula.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent verb/title double meaning.

hints.reason: SPOT via spotlight; STAGE via stage lights, and the two phrases converge since a spotlight is a stage light.

pairs.pair_note: Easy phrase-join that converges on one object; plain but satisfying enough.

hints.reason: TOWER via a turret as a small castle tower; TANK via the rotating gun turret.

pairs.pair_note: Accurate, fair, nicely etymological (the tank turret is named after the tower).
